Package org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.prefs

Class HolidayRegions

java.lang.Object
org.jdesktop.lg3d.utils.prefs.HolidayRegions
public final class HolidayRegions extends Object
The single source of truth for turning a configured holiday-region token into a statutory-holiday list, shared by every surface that marks holidays: the 2D taskbar clock's calendar popup (via HolidayCalendar) and the orgchart AgendaGrid. It lives in lg3d-core because the Gradle module dependency direction (incubator -> core) forbids the two callers from sharing a helper placed in either app module.

The region is a small token grammar: "AUTO" (the DesktopConfig default) derives the holiday set from the system Locale — Canada maps to Canadian federal, everything else to US federal — while an explicit token overrides it: "US" or "CA" (federal), "CA:<PROVINCE>" (e.g. "CA:QUEBEC") or "US:<STATE>". The Control Center's Desktop panel edits that token and persists it, so both the calendar and the agenda reflect the user's choice across restarts.

Every method is static, pure and defensive: resolveRegion(java.lang.String, java.util.Locale) and holidays(java.lang.String, int) are unit-testable headless, and a holiday/weekend lookup never throws — if jbusinessday (or its slf4j dependency) is missing at runtime, or a token names an unknown province/state, the day is simply treated as an ordinary day rather than breaking the caller. Memoisation of each year's list is left to the caller (the two callers keep their own caches).

      public static String resolveRegion(String configured, Locale locale)
      Resolves a configured token to an effective one: a blank/AUTO value falls back to the locale's country (Canada -> "CA", otherwise "US"); any explicit token is normalised (trimmed, upper-cased) and returned as-is. Pure so the mapping is unit-testable.

    • holidays

      public static List<LocalDate> holidays(String token, int year)
      The statutory holidays token selects for year. Pure and defensive: an unknown token or a missing jbusinessday/slf4j runtime yields an empty list rather than throwing, so the caller still renders.
